statement: For every field K and every integer c >= 2, in K[x,y,z] the ideal I_c=(x^2,y^2,z^c,xyz) satisfies v(I_c)=2 and v(overline(I_c))=ceil(c/2). Consequently v(overline(I_2))<v(I_2), equality holds for c=3,4, and v(I_c)<v(overline(I_c)) holds exactly for c>=5.
contribution: A field-independent weighted Newton-polyhedron argument and complete symbolic socle classification prove the frozen all-parameter claim, extending the supplied primary paper's single c=5 example to every c>=2 and resolving all endpoint regimes. The literature comparison is bounded and makes no priority claim.
